```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Price floor: every listed competitor in B charges from the start. NeverFined starts at $29/mo, ExpirationOps runs a 14-day trial then $49/mo, and ClearBot charges $500+/location/yr. In A, Zigpoll (free to 50 responses), Fairing (free to 200 orders) and Compra (free to 100 responses) all have free-forever tiers. A new entrant in A would likely need a free tier too, which pushes back the first paying customer. That matters most for a 90-day target.",
    "Demand breadth: B cites three independent Reddit posts from different roles (a solo structural engineer, an HR practitioner, a therapist) describing multi-state licensing pain. A cites one merchant post plus a competitor's founder story. The competitor story proves the market can be won, not that a new entrant will find demand.",
    "Price ceiling: B's sourced tiers run from $29/mo to $500-800/location/yr to $3,999-$10,000+/yr for enterprise services. That shows buyers pay real money and leaves room to price above the cheapest trackers. A is anchored at $25-49/mo against free alternatives.",
    "Launch timeline: A's own brief says the category leader took two years to gain traction. It also says merchants expect reviews and trust signals before granting order-data access, which a zero-review app cannot have in 90 days. B's 'tracking only, not advice' approach needs one attorney consult and no marketplace trust ramp.",
    "Shared weaknesses: neither idea has a demonstrated wedge, and both face crowded SEO channels. B's paid CPC is higher ($10-14.50 vs ~$6). But A's built-in App Store discovery mostly delivers free installs, so the cheaper clicks do not clearly reach a paying customer faster."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence is one Reddit post. The brief infers 'existing willingness to pay for an automated tool' from it, but the merchant never says they would pay. The only other demand signal is a seed-quote success story from a direct competitor, which shows the market is already served rather than showing unmet demand for a new entrant.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with no sourced wedge. B's demand quotes partly concern individual professional licensure (engineer, therapist), not the 'finance/ops lead at a multi-state business' payer the brief targets, so the fit is imperfect. B's claim that thin trackers like ExpirationOps and NeverFined reach paying customers is an inference ('appear to be'), not sourced revenue. B also carries an ongoing data-freshness burden. The pick rests mainly on B's paid-from-day-one price floor versus A's free-tier compression, given the 90-day paying-customer goal."
}
```
